tunnels.accessIntroRaw: On TCP/UDP tunnels, access is controlled by the IP allowlist and by web door. The sign-in method below is used on the door page to verify the visitor.

tunnels.protocolIntro: The protocol this tunnel carries. HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket are supported today.
tunnels.protoHttpHint: Websites, APIs and WebSocket connections. Automatic TLS.
tunnels.protoTcpHint: Raw TCP services like Minecraft Java, SSH, databases — via subdomain + TLS-SNI.
tunnels.exposurePortHint: Visitors connect directly to {domain}:PORT. Ideal for Minecraft.
tunnels.exposureSniHint: No extra ports; visitors run the 'zorven forward' command.
tunnels.exposureGuidePort: Reserved port: game servers (Minecraft etc.), SSH/RDP and anything where visitors must connect directly with no setup. The address is host:PORT; some school/corporate networks block high ports. This is the only option for UDP.
tunnels.exposureGuideSni: SNI + forwarder: networks that block high ports, and many tunnels. It uses no extra port (goes over 443) but visitors must run the "zorven forward" command; raw game clients cannot connect directly.
tunnels.exposureGuideUdp: Not sure? Use Reserved port for games and UDP, SNI for TCP services reached from corporate networks. Your plan may limit the number of reserved ports; deleting unused tunnels frees the port (it is reissued after a short cooling-off period).
tunnels.sniUdpUnavailable: SNI for UDP isn't available yet; use a reserved port for UDP.
tunnels.connectPortPending: A port will be assigned after saving (once the data plane is enabled).
tunnels.connectSniHint: The visitor runs this command and connects to the local port.
tunnels.protocolDataPlaneNote: Note: the protocol choice is saved; the TCP/UDP data plane (traffic transport) will be enabled in a following update.
tunnels.ipIntro: Only the listed IPs/CIDRs can reach this tunnel. Empty means open to all.
tunnels.ipEmpty: No IP restriction — tunnel is open to all IPs.
tunnels.accessPassKeepHint: A password is set. Leave blank to keep the current one.
tunnels.sessionTtlHint: How long a visitor stays signed in before having to log in again (15 minutes - 30 days). Shortening it also applies to existing sessions.
tunnels.sessionSlidingHint: When on, an active visitor's session is extended automatically once more than half of it has elapsed. It can last at most 7 days after the first sign-in (or the session length, if longer).
tunnels.sessionRevokeHint: Affected visitors must sign in again. Later sign-ins are not affected.
tunnels.sessionRevokeAllConfirm: End all visitor sessions for this tunnel?
tunnels.accessUserRequired: Username is required for Basic Auth.
tunnels.accessPassRequired: Password is required for Basic Auth.
tunnels.noClients: No clients yet. Connect a device first with the zorven CLI.
tunnels.lbIntro: Choose how requests are spread across replicas. With health checks on, a replica that fails its check is taken out of rotation and brought back once it recovers.
tunnels.lbStrategyHint_round_robin: Requests rotate across online replicas in turn.
tunnels.lbStrategyHint_weighted: Each replica gets a share proportional to its weight. A weight of 0 is used only when the others are unreachable.
tunnels.lbStrategyHint_least_connections: A new request goes to the replica with the fewest open requests right now.
tunnels.lbStrategyHint_latency: Picks the replica with the lowest latency measured by health checks. Turning health checks on is recommended.
tunnels.lbPanicHint: If every replica looks unhealthy, traffic is spread across all online replicas so service doesn't stop entirely.

tunnels.rawQualityHint: Latency and loss between the server and the client, measured by a probe every 5 seconds. The client-to-local-service leg is not measured.
tunnels.rawQualityUnsupported: Client version does not support this: update the client to measure latency and loss.
tunnels.rawQualityNone: No measurements yet; they appear within a few minutes while the client is connected.
tunnels.rawLimitsHint: Each source address counts as one connection. Packets over a limit are dropped silently and show up in the stats. Limits other than the defaults are available on Pro and above.
tunnels.rawGameHint: The query goes straight to your server through the tunnel and doesn't touch visitor traffic. Available on Pro and above.

mcp.title: Connect with MCP (Claude, Cursor)
mcp.desc: Connect Zorven to AI assistants as an MCP server: read devices, tunnels, domains and request logs, and create tunnels and domains through the assistant. There are no delete tools.
mcp.step1: Create an API key above. Read-only needs the *:read scopes; add tunnels:write and hostnames:write to create tunnels and domains.
mcp.step2: Tools for scopes the key does not have are never shown to the assistant.
mcp.step3: Copy one of the examples below and replace YOUR_API_KEY with your key.
mcp.claudeWebSteps: Open Claude > Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector, paste the endpoint above and sign in with your Zorven account. You choose the organization and permissions on the consent screen (read-only is the default). Manage connections under the 'Connected apps' tab.
mcp.note: For local use install the zorven client; 'zorven mcp' runs over stdio. Details: docs/mcp.md. Claude web and desktop connect with OAuth: no API key needed.

terminal.errOffline: This client is not online; the terminal cannot be opened.
terminal.shellWarn: This runs a real shell on the remote machine. The commands you type are executed on that machine.
terminal.shellWarnPost: on the remote machine. The commands you type are executed on that machine.
terminal.reconnectedNote: — reconnected; a new shell session was started —
terminal.errGaveUp: Could not reconnect to the server.
terminal.maxTabs: At most {n} tabs can be open
terminal.takenOver: This session was opened in another browser tab.

mail.title: Webmail
mail.subtitle: Mail delivered to your {domain} address, plus reply and send.
mail.disabled: Webmail is not configured on this server yet. It activates once the admin sets an MX record for {domain} and opens the inbound (25) port.
mail.subject: Subject
mail.deleteConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this message?

mailApps.disabled: Mail app access (IMAP/SMTP) is not enabled on this server yet. It becomes available once the administrator sets up the TLS certificate and opens ports 993 / 587 / 465.
mailApps.intro: You can use your mailbox in a mail app such as the Gmail app, Outlook, Apple Mail or Thunderbird. Instead of your account password, you enter an app password that you create below.
mailApps.gmailWebNote: Google is discontinuing the "Check mail from other accounts (POP3)" feature in Gmail on the web. We therefore recommend the Gmail mobile app (Android / iOS) or an IMAP client.
mailApps.passwordNote: Password: the app password you create below (your normal account password will not work).
mailApps.label: Label
mailApps.createdHint: This password is shown only now. Paste it into your app; spaces and dashes do not matter. If you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
mailApps.revokeConfirm: Revoke the app password "{label}"? Apps using this password will no longer be able to connect.
mailApps.createFailed: Could not create the app password.
mailApps.revokeFailed: Could not revoke the app password.
mailApps.profileNote: The profile contains no password; you enter the app password during setup. It is unsigned, so your device may show a warning.

gmail.title: Gmail app
gmail.intro: The Gmail mobile app for Android and iOS.
gmail.s1: Open the Gmail app, tap your profile picture at the top right and choose "Add another account".
gmail.s3: Enter {address} as the email address and continue.
gmail.s5: Paste the app password you created above as the password. If asked for the incoming server: {host}, port {imap}, SSL/TLS.
gmail.s6: For the outgoing server enter {host}, port {smtp} (STARTTLS), username {address} and the same app password; keep "Require sign-in" on, then finish.

outlook.title: Outlook
outlook.intro: Outlook for desktop (Windows / Mac) and mobile.
outlook.s1: Desktop: go to File > Add Account, enter {address} and under "Advanced options" tick "Let me set up my account manually". Mobile: Settings > Add account > Add email account.
outlook.s2: Choose IMAP as the account type.
outlook.s4: Outgoing mail: {host}, port {smtp}, encryption STARTTLS (alternative: port 465, SSL/TLS).
outlook.s5: Username: {address}. Password: the app password. Click Connect.

apple.title: Apple Mail
apple.s1: Easiest: download and open the profile below (iPhone/iPad: Settings > General > VPN & Device Management; Mac: System Settings > Profiles).
apple.s2: Or manually: Settings > Mail > Accounts > Add Account > Other > Add Mail Account (Mac: Mail > Add Account > Other Mail Account).
apple.s3: Enter your name, the address {address} and the app password.
apple.s4: Choose IMAP as the account type. Incoming and outgoing server: {host}.
apple.s5: On both servers use {address} as the username and the app password as the password (outgoing: port {smtp}, SSL), then tap Save.

thunderbird.title: Thunderbird
thunderbird.s1: Open Account Settings > Account Actions > Add Mail Account.
thunderbird.s2: Enter your name, the address {address} and the app password; press Continue.
thunderbird.s3: Thunderbird detects the server {host} (IMAP {imap} SSL/TLS, SMTP {smtp} STARTTLS). If it cannot, choose "Configure manually" and enter these values.
thunderbird.s4: Make sure the username is the full address ({address}) and press Done.

secrets.title: Secret Vault
secrets.subtitle: Centrally manage encrypted secrets. Values are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and shown only once at creation.
secrets.empty: No secrets yet. Create your first one.
secrets.usageHint: Reference in policy and webhook configs:
secrets.revealHint: This value is shown only now. Save it somewhere safe — it won't be shown again.

policies.title: Policy Engine
policies.subtitle: Edge gateway rules: match → action. Rate limit, deny, redirect, headers and mTLS in one engine.
policies.empty: No policies yet. Create your first one.
policies.name: Name
policies.mtlsHint: Returns 403 if the request does not carry a verified client certificate (mTLS).
policies.setHeaderHint: Request/response headers are set via JSON config (request.set / response.set).
policies.geoWarning: Geo and IP list conditions are not a security gate on their own: VPNs, proxies and shared exits change the result. Use them alongside authentication, not instead of it. If the database or list is not configured, the condition does not match and the request flows normally.
policies.webhookHint: Supply the secret through the Secret Vault using a secret reference (the format shown in the placeholder); do not paste plaintext. If the signature does not verify, the request never reaches the tunnel. At most 1 MB of body is buffered; larger bodies get 413.
policies.patternsPh: One regex per line (organization-specific extra patterns)
policies.wafHint: The owasp-lite set scans the path, query and selected headers; the request body is not scanned. An invalid regex drops the rule — it stays listed but does not run.
policies.challengeHint: Sends the visitor to the tunnel's OAuth sign-in. If visitor OAuth is not configured on the server, the request is denied (403).

org.title: Organization and projects
org.subtitle: Manage your organization and projects here.
org.name: Organization name
org.slugFixed: the short name cannot change (it is used in tunnel addresses)
org.projectsHint: When a project is deleted, its tunnels, domains and clients move to the default project. A project that still holds secrets, policies or log sinks cannot be deleted; remove those first.
org.projectDeleteConfirm: Delete project "{name}"? Its tunnels, domains and clients move to the default project.
org.deleteExplain: This cannot be undone. All clients, tunnels, domains, projects, secrets, policies, API tokens and request logs of the organization are deleted; connected agents are disconnected and tunnels go offline. Only an owner or admin can do this.
org.cannotDeleteDefault: The platform organization cannot be deleted.
org.cannotDeleteLast: This is the only organization you belong to. Create another one before deleting it.
org.deleteFinalConfirm: "{slug}" and all its data will be permanently deleted. Are you sure?
org.projectLimitReached: Your plan allows at most {n} projects.

network.title: Private network
network.subtitle: Secure access to internal resources (databases, SSH, NAS) without exposing them to the internet.
network.step1: Create an API token with at least the "tunnels:read" scope on the API & Security page.
network.step2: Run this command on your own computer; it opens a SOCKS5 proxy at 127.0.0.1:1080:
network.step3: Use 127.0.0.1:1080 as the SOCKS5 proxy in your application and connect to the resource by name (e.g. db.internal:5432).
network.limits: This is the first stage: only TCP and SOCKS5-capable applications work; ping (ICMP) and UDP are not supported yet. Access to a resource equals access to the device that publishes it (Device access policies).
network.deleteConfirm: Delete private resource "{name}"? Open connections to it will close.
network.addHint: The target is the address as seen from the selected device (e.g. localhost:5432 for a database on the same machine, 192.168.1.10:22 for a server on the local network). The resource is not exposed to the internet; no hostname or public port is assigned.
network.subnetHint: Publishes an address range from the selected device's local network (e.g. 192.168.1.0/24). Authorized users reach IPs in this range with zorven connect. Only private ranges (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 100.64/10, fc00::/7) can be published; the device also independently checks that the target is within the range.

consent.title: Authorize application
consent.intro: {name} wants to connect to your Zorven account and use the Zorven MCP server on your behalf.
consent.unverified: This application is not verified by Zorven. Only approve connections you started yourself.
consent.redirectTo: After you decide you will be sent to {host}.
consent.orgHint: The application can only access the organization you select.
consent.readOnlyHint: The application can view devices, tunnels, domains and logs, but cannot create or change anything.
consent.noDelete: Delete operations are never available to the application.
consent.noOrgs: You are not a member of any organization.
consent.errLogin: Sign in with your Zorven account (not an admin key) to authorize an application.
consent.errGeneric: The request could not be completed. Please try again.
consent.tunnelHint: The application will call this MCP server with your Zorven account as its identity. The server owner can see your email.
consent.tunnelDenied: {email} is not allowed to use this MCP server. Ask its owner to add you.
consent.destructiveHint: These let the application permanently delete things. Enable only if you really need it.
consent.fullWarn: If you enable this, the application can do everything you can do in the Zorven panel with your account and role: read and change tunnels, domains, policies, team, mail, billing views and more.
consent.fullTick: Grant full access to this application
consent.fullRequested: This application asked for full access. It is only granted if you tick the box.
consent.fullLimits: Never available, even with full access: creating or managing API tokens, service accounts and app passwords, approving device logins, changing sign-in credentials, and deleting the organization. Access ends after 30 minutes unless renewed (renewal lasts at most 7 days between uses and 30 days in total) and you can revoke it any time under Connected apps.
consent.fullReauthBody: Full access needs a fresh sign-in (password, and two-factor code if enabled) within the last 5 minutes. You will return to this page after signing in.
consent.errReauth: Full access needs a fresh sign-in. Sign in again and retry.

scope.mcp_read: Read your devices, tunnels, domains and request logs
scope.mcp_manage: Read everything and create or update tunnels and domains (no deleting)
scope.mcp: Use this MCP server on your behalf
scope.tunnels_delete: Permanently delete tunnels (asks for the tunnel name each time)
scope.hostnames_delete: Permanently delete domains (asks for the domain each time)
scope.full: Full access: everything you can do in the Zorven panel (with your role)

apps.title: Connected apps
apps.desc: Applications you authorized with OAuth, for example the Claude custom connector. Revoking cuts off access within about a minute.
apps.emptyHint: Add Zorven as a custom connector in Claude and it will show up here.
apps.needAccount: Connected apps are only available when signed in with an account (not an admin key).

invite.title: Team Invitation
invite.body: {who} invited you to the {org} organization as {role}.
invite.accessNote: If you accept, you can access this organization's tunnels, devices and all other sections. Your own organizations are not affected.
invite.errNotFound: Invitation not found. The link may be wrong or the invitation was canceled.
invite.errEmailMismatch: This invitation was sent to a different email address. You are signed in as {email}; sign in with the invited address.
invite.errExpired: This invitation has expired. Ask the team admin for a new one.
invite.errClosed: This invitation is no longer valid (already accepted, declined or canceled).
invite.errSession: Sign in with your own account to accept the invitation.

updatesAdmin.title: Updates
updatesAdmin.subtitle: Release notes, updates and maintenance notices. Published posts appear on the public page.
updatesAdmin.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes. E.g. release-0-2-9
updatesAdmin.mHint: Times are entered in your local time and stored as UTC.
updatesAdmin.bodyHint: Headings (#), lists (-), **bold**, *italic*, `code`, [link](https://...) are supported. Raw HTML is ignored.
updatesAdmin.trRequired: Turkish is required; if EN/JA are empty visitors see Turkish/English.
updatesAdmin.slugTaken: This address is used by another post.
updatesAdmin.testFailed: Could not send the test email.
updatesAdmin.sendConfirmBody: This post will be emailed to {n} users with a verified email who opted in to product announcements. Make sure you checked the test email first.
updatesAdmin.sendConfirmForce: This post was already sent. Sending again emails the same people a second time.
updatesAdmin.resumeBody: Sending continues only with recipients who have not received this post yet. People who already got it are skipped.
updatesAdmin.retryBody: Only the {f} emails that failed will be tried again. Everyone else is left alone.
updatesAdmin.interruptedHint: The server restarted while sending. Nothing resumes automatically; press Resume to continue with the remaining recipients.
updatesAdmin.failedHint: {f} emails could not be delivered. You can retry just those.
updatesAdmin.nothingToResume: There is nothing to resume or retry for this post.
updatesAdmin.importHint: Paste a single post object, an array of posts or an object with a "posts" array, or pick a .json file. Unknown fields are rejected. Importing never sends email.
updatesAdmin.importPublishHint: When off, every post is imported as a draft.
updatesAdmin.importNeedPreview: Run a preview first; import once the results look right.
updatesAdmin.importDone: Import finished: {create} created, {update} updated, {skip} skipped, {error} with errors.

shares.title: Shares
shares.subtitle: Share a device port end-to-end encrypted (WireGuard) with the people, groups or devices you choose. The server cannot see the content; no admin rights needed.
shares.howShare: Sharer: create a share on this page, or run zorven share <port> --to <recipient> on the device.
shares.howAccess: Recipient: run this command with an API token, then connect via 127.0.0.1:
shares.emptyIncoming: Nothing has been shared with you.
shares.revokeConfirm: Revoke share "{name}"? Access is cut immediately.
shares.name: Name (optional)
shares.unavailable: Zorven Net is disabled on this server.
shares.relayNote: Connections start through the server (relay) and switch to a direct encrypted path between devices (P2P) when possible. Either way the server cannot decrypt the content.
shares.pathDirectHint: Direct encrypted connection between devices (P2P); traffic does not pass through the server.
shares.pathRelayHint: A direct connection could not be established (NAT/firewall); traffic is relayed through the server, encrypted.
shares.pathMixedHint: Some recipients are connected directly, others via relay.

nettun.title: Full network layer (Mode B)
nettun.subtitle: Join this device to the tenant's private network with a real network interface (TUN): peers reach each other by IP or by <device>.zorven.internal. Access follows the rules below; everything not allowed is dropped.
nettun.howUp: On the device: sudo zorven net up (Windows: elevated PowerShell, zorven net up). Requires the Zorven service.
nettun.howDown: To leave the network: zorven net down. Port sharing (Mode A) keeps working either way.
nettun.nodesEmpty: No device has opened Mode B yet.
nettun.otherNodes: {n} more node(s) use port sharing only (Mode A)
nettun.networkHint: Pool: {cidr} · virtual DNS: {resolver}. If this range overlaps a local interface (for example Tailscale), Mode B refuses to start; pick another range here.
nettun.networkLocked: The range can only be changed while no device is registered in the network.
nettun.rulesIntro: Default: nothing is allowed (default deny). A rule opens traffic from a source device to a destination device. Replies to connections a device starts itself are always accepted.
nettun.rulesEmpty: No rules yet; devices in Mode B cannot reach each other.
nettun.adminOnly: Only organization owners and admins can manage access rules.
nettun.loadError: Could not load full network layer data.
nettun.dnsNote: Names: <device>.zorven.internal. The resolver runs on the device (no DNS query leaves it); only *.zorven.internal is handled, all other names use your normal DNS.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.desc: The page you are looking for may have moved, been deleted, or never existed.
notFound.errorDesc: An unexpected error occurred. Try reloading the page.

mcpTunnel.intro: Publish this tunnel as a protected MCP server. Zorven adds sign-in (OAuth or API key), keeps streams unbuffered, can allow or block individual tools and logs calls (metadata only, never arguments or results).
mcpTunnel.loadFailed: MCP settings could not be loaded.
mcpTunnel.saveFailed: MCP settings could not be saved.
mcpTunnel.claudeSteps: Claude: Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector > paste the URL. Other clients:
mcpTunnel.noUrl: This tunnel has no active domain yet; add one in Domains to get a connection URL.
mcpTunnel.authOauth: OAuth (recommended): sign in with a Zorven account
mcpTunnel.authNone: None: anyone with the URL (not recommended)
mcpTunnel.oauthUnavailable: The OAuth server is not enabled on this installation. Use API keys.
mcpTunnel.oauthHelp: Clients sign in through Zorven. Access is limited to the people below. Anyone else is rejected before reaching your server.
mcpTunnel.allowedEmailsHelp: One per line. *@example.com allows a whole domain. The Zorven account must have a verified email. An empty list allows nobody besides the members above.
mcpTunnel.revokeConfirm: End all OAuth sessions connected to this MCP server? Clients must sign in again.
mcpTunnel.apikeyHelp: Clients send the key as Authorization: Bearer or X-API-Key. Keys are shown once and stored only as a hash.
mcpTunnel.keyShownOnce: Copy this key now. It will not be shown again.
mcpTunnel.keyDeleteConfirm: Delete key "{name}"? Clients using it lose access immediately.
mcpTunnel.noneWarn: Anyone on the internet who knows the URL can call every tool of this server. Make sure it exposes nothing sensitive.
mcpTunnel.noneAck: I understand and want to publish it without authentication
mcpTunnel.policyHelp: One tool name or pattern per line (* and ? wildcards). Deny wins. If the allow list is not empty, only listed tools can be called and are shown in tools/list. Blocked calls get a JSON-RPC error and never reach your server.
mcpTunnel.legacyNote: Old HTTP+SSE transport (2024-11-05): calls are blocked, but the tool list cannot be filtered because it travels on a separate stream. Tools that run arbitrary commands by name are not protected by name lists.
mcpTunnel.testFailed: The test could not be run.
mcpTunnel.privacy: Only method, tool name, status and duration are logged. Arguments and results are never stored.

privnet.title: Private resources (zero trust)
privnet.subtitle: Which policy opens which private resource (for example db.internal) to whom. Devices in Mode B reach a resource by name over the private network; people and service accounts use the browser or zorven connect.
privnet.resEmpty: No private resource yet. Create one on the Private network page and pick the device that publishes it.
privnet.hostNotModeB: Not in Mode B: devices cannot reach it over the private network
privnet.noDevices: No policy opens this resource to devices in Mode B.
privnet.noPeople: No policy names people or service accounts (owners and admins always have access).
privnet.skipped: {n} policy(ies) skipped in Mode B: person conditions (two-factor, IP range) cannot be evaluated for a device.
privnet.retention: Kept for {d} days. Denied flows are also written to the audit log.
privnet.adminOnly: Only owners and admins can see this.
privnet.loadError: Could not load private network access.

howto.title: Turning on the full network layer
howto.what: The full network layer (Mode B) adds a virtual network interface to your device. Reach authorized peers by IP address or <device>.zorven.internal from any app.
howto.cliNote: The client must be connected. On Linux the service has CAP_NET_ADMIN when installed with 'zorven up'.
howto.desktop: Use the On/Off button on the app's 'Full network layer' card. The app must run as Administrator; it offers to restart elevated if needed.
howto.driver: The Windows driver (wintun) is downloaded automatically and is signed.
howto.access: Access is governed by this page's access rules and policies.

tunsec.intro: Tunnel-level protection: WAF rules and country (Geo) restrictions. They run before sign-in, so even the login surface is protected.
tunsec.planNotice: WAF block mode and country rules require the Pro plan or higher. Log mode is available on every plan; on lower plans block mode behaves as log mode and country rules are not enforced.
tunsec.modeHelp_log: Requests pass; matches are recorded in the request log.
tunsec.modeHelp_block: Matching requests get 403 and a request ID.
tunsec.scanBody: Also scan the request body (first 8 KB)
tunsec.scanBodyHint: Only form, JSON and text bodies. Off by default; may raise false positives for code or markdown editors.
tunsec.rulesHint: Click a group to turn it off (strikethrough). Use this if a group causes false positives for your app.
tunsec.geoHelp_allow: Only the listed countries can connect.
tunsec.countriesHint: Comma separated two-letter codes, e.g. TR, DE, US.
tunsec.geoNote: Applies to HTTP and to raw TCP/UDP connections. Open connections are re-evaluated when you save.
tunsec.geoDbMissing: No Geo database is loaded on this server, so every country is "unknown". Ask your administrator to install the GeoLite2-Country file.
tunsec.blockedEmpty: No blocked or observed requests yet.

tunbot.botIntro: Shows visitors a short browser check (proof-of-work). Visitors see a "Verifying your browser" page for a few seconds, then continue to the site; bots and simple scripts cannot pass.
tunbot.modeHelp_suspicious: Only visitors that look suspicious see the verification.
tunbot.modeHelp_always: "I'm under attack" mode: every visitor sees the verification.
tunbot.diffHint_strong: 20 bits, about 2-8 s (longer on weak devices)
tunbot.ttlHint: A verified visitor is not asked again for this long (__zv_bot cookie).
tunbot.excludeHintBot: APIs, webhooks and app clients cannot solve the verification page. Add their paths (e.g. /api/*, /webhook/*) here.
tunbot.excludeHintRate: These paths are not counted by the rate limit.
tunbot.excludeErrStar: "*" is only allowed at the end of the path.
tunbot.excludeErrMax: At most 32 paths can be added.
tunbot.verifiedBotsHint: Bots such as Googlebot and Bingbot (verified by reverse+forward DNS) pass without verification.
tunbot.blockEmptyUa: Block requests with an empty User-Agent
tunbot.blockEmptyUaHint: Requests that send no browser identity are rejected outright.
tunbot.visitorNote: Visitors see a short "Verifying your browser" page and continue automatically. Non-browser clients (APIs, webhooks) get 403/429 with an X-Zorven-Challenge: required header instead of the page; exclude them.
tunbot.rateIntro: Counts requests per IP within a window; clients over the limit are blocked or sent to the verification.
tunbot.errWindow: Window must be between 1 and 3600 s.
tunbot.planNotice: Verify-everyone mode and rate limiting require the Pro plan or higher. On lower plans "everyone" behaves as "suspicious" and the rate limit is not enforced; your settings are kept.
tunbot.statsNote: Successful passes are not logged. "+" means the count reached the page limit.
tunbot.invalid: Invalid bot protection / rate limit settings.

captcha.title: Zorven CAPTCHA
captcha.subtitle: A cookieless, tracking-free verification widget that protects your forms from bots. Embed the site key in your page and verify with the secret on your server.
captcha.empty: You have no CAPTCHA sites yet. Create your first one.
captcha.deleteConfirm: Delete site "{name}"? Forms using it will no longer verify.
captcha.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret for "{name}"? The old secret stops working immediately.
captcha.embedHint: Load the script once and place the widget inside your form. On submit, the hidden "zorven-captcha-response" field reaches your server.
captcha.verifyHint: Keep the secret on your server only (environment variable). A response is single-use and valid for 5 minutes.
captcha.privacyNote: By default no cookies are used and visitors are not tracked. If the pass cookie is enabled, only a first-party cookie with no personal data is written.
captcha.domainsHint: Leave empty to allow any domain. "example.com" also covers subdomains.
captcha.domainErrMax: You can add at most 50 domains.
captcha.passHint: When on, a first-party cookie with no personal data (zcap_pass) is written on your site's domain after verification; repeat checks become faster until it expires and visitor metrics are recorded.
captcha.secretWarn: The secret key is shown only now and cannot be displayed again. Store it somewhere safe; if you lose it you must rotate it.
